UIElement

UIElement is the base class for all MelonUI controls. It provides the common properties for layout, styling, focus, data binding and element lifetime.

Common Properties

  • Name / UID: Name is used for looking up an element. UID identifies a particular instance and does not change.
  • Children / Parent / ParentWindow: The elements owned by this element and the page/window it belongs to. Ownership is managed through the collections.
  • IsVisible / IsEnabled: Controls display and availability. IsEffectivelyVisible and IsEffectivelyEnabled also include the parent state.
  • ConsiderForFocus / TabIndex: Controls whether the element is included in focus navigation and its order among siblings. IsFocused is managed by the window.
  • LockControls: Prevents the control from responding to its normal input.
  • EnableCaching: Allows the rendered buffer to be reused until the element changes.

Common Methods

  • Find<T> / FindById: Looks up a descendant by its name or UID.
  • Remove: Detaches the element without destroying it. RequestRemove can queue this on the UI thread.
  • Dispose: Removes the element and permanently cleans up its children, bindings and resources.
  • Invalidate: Requests a new render for the element and its parents.
  • SetBinding / RemoveBinding: Adds or removes a binding for a property.
  • TryHandleKey / RegisterKeyboardControl: Handles input or registers a control-specific shortcut.

Creating a Derived Class

UIElement is abstract. To create a control, derive from it and implement RenderContent:

The base Render method prepares the buffer and draws the border. RenderContent draws inside that buffer. See the Custom Controls Guide for a complete example with input handling and generated properties.

Updating the Display

Generated UI properties invalidate their element when changed. If you change other state that affects drawing, call Invalidate yourself. An animated control can set EnableCaching=false so it is rendered continuously.

UIElement owns its Children collection, but it does not automatically draw the children. A container must lay out and combine their buffers. Use MUIPage if you only need normal page composition.
